Relevant excerpt: "In line with previous research (e.g., Hatoum & Belle, 2004; Slater & Tiggemann, 2006), participants indicated the number of hours spent, on average, (a) watching television each day; (b) looking at magazines each month; (c) using the Internet during the week; and (d) using the Internet on weekends, from 1 = 0 h to 8 = 6+ hours. Question (b) was assessed by type (fashion, health/fitness, sports, men's interest, gay). Item scores were averaged for each form of media separately; higher scores reflect higher levels of consumption of television, magazines, and Internet, respectively."

section_summary.extract_value: This section describes how media consumption was measured: participants reported hours spent watching television (daily), looking at magazines (monthly, by type), and using the Internet (weekday and weekend) on an 8-point scale (1 = 0 h to 8 = 6+ hours). Item scores were averaged separately for television, magazines (by type: fashion, health/fitness, sports, men's interest, gay), and Internet, with higher scores indicating greater consumption. The section does not reference 'Study 1' or any numbered studies nor provide sample, demographic, BMI, or correlation data.
